content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication abacavir, but it does not include all possible details. It is important to note that this information does not guarantee the safety, effectiveness, or appropriateness of the medication for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Important Warning: Abacavir can cause a severe, potentially fatal allergic reaction in some individuals. Before starting or restarting this medication, your doctor should perform a blood test to assess your risk. If the test indicates a higher risk, you should not take abacavir, and your doctor will discuss alternative treatments. Symptoms of an allergic reaction may include rash, itching or swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, difficulty breathing, fever, extreme fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, muscle aches, sore throat, or cough. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek medical attention immediately. If you have stopped taking abacavir due to an allergic reaction, you must never take it again, as this could result in death. Inform all your doctors and pharmacists if you have discontinued abacavir for this reason. Additionally, properly dispose of any unused abacavir. Uses: Abacavir is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, abacavir is not a cure for HIV. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity and avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or bodily fluids. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide and Warning Card provided by your pharmacist before starting abacavir and each time you get a refill. Carry the Warning Card with you at all times. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking abacavir, even for a short time, and then restart it, you are at an increased risk of developing a severe, potentially fatal allergic reaction. Refill your medication before running out, and do not stop treatment unless directed by your doctor. It is crucial to take abacavir and other HIV medications exactly as prescribed. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, or take it more frequently than prescribed. For the best effect, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Side Effects: Common side effects may include trouble sleeping or loss of appetite. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time during treatment, even months later. Rarely, abacavir has been associated with severe, potentially fatal liver problems and a buildup of lactic acid in the blood (lactic acidosis). These side effects are more common in women and obese patients. If you experience symptoms such as persistent nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or rapid breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Precautions: Before taking abacavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Abacavir may increase your risk of a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as ways to lower your risk of heart disease. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of passing HIV to your baby. Abacavir passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, nonprescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not take abacavir with other medications that contain abacavir. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store abacavir tablets or solution at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The solution may also be stored in the refrigerator but should not be frozen. Over time, the solution may change color from clear or yellow to brown, which is normal. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. Monitoring: Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and complete information about this medication.
